messages:
maria: Heads-up — customer (acct ID redwood-corp) reporting intermittent 504s and long tail latency on /v1/generate. They use redwood-go-sdk v0.9.5 with a custom http.Client. Root request timestamp 2241200000.

maria: Short repro notes from them: sudden 504s after ~5s, then context canceled errors in app logs. They see a spike after token refresh.

derek: Can you paste the app log around a failure? also what Go version + os?

maria: log snippet: 
```
2026-03-16T12:06:21Z ERROR request failed status=504 err="context canceled" id=abc123
2026-03-16T12:06:21Z DEBUG http: request canceled while waiting for connection
2026-03-16T12:06:22Z INFO token refresh start
2026-03-16T12:06:22Z INFO token refresh complete
```
They run go1.20.4 on linux.

raj: two quick suspects: (1) mismatch between http.Client.Timeout and the request context deadline (dual cancellation), (2) token refresh middleware that rebuilds Transport on each refresh causing stale connections / broken reuse.

timothy: Example problematic pattern we see a lot:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, bytes.NewReader(body))
client := &http.Client{
  Timeout: 15 * time.Second, // > ctx deadline
  Transport: &http.Transport{
    MaxIdleConns: 100,
    IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
  },
}
resp, err := client.Do(req)
```
With client.Timeout > ctx deadline you get reactive client-side timeouts + context cancellations racing; also creating a new Transport per token refresh prevents connection reuse and can exhaust sockets.

sylvie: Recommended guidance: either rely on context and set client.Timeout=0 OR set client.Timeout <= context deadline. Prefer: client.Timeout=0 and control with ctx. Also ensure transport is shared (single Transport instance) and not rebuilt per request. Set IdleConnTimeout and MaxIdleConnsPerHost appropriately.

maria: Customer confirmed they recreate the SDK on token refresh (so new Transport each time). They also had retry middleware that wrapped Do and used context.Background() for retries (so ignoring original ctx). Bad combo.

derek: Short mitigation steps for customer: 1) upgrade to redwood-go-sdk v1.4.0 (fixes retry wrapper to respect request ctx and exposes WithTransport option), 2) stop recreating Transport on every token refresh — instead use a long-lived transport and swap credentials via RoundTripper that reads token from atomic.Value, 3) set client.Timeout=0 and control via context deadlines, 4) add instrumentation: dump net/http/pprof and track socket counts.

raj: For support response, ask for: Go env, SDK version, copy of http.Transport settings, minimal snippet that reproduces, and network trace (tcp conn states) if possible. Also ask if they're using HTTP/2 (we've seen GOAWAY when token rotates).

maria: Customer asked for quick workaround while they upgrade. I suggested: set SDK option WithTransport(&http.Transport{MaxIdleConns:50, MaxIdleConnsPerHost:50, IdleConnTimeout:30*time.Second, DisableKeepAlives:false}) and ensure token refresh updates a header via middleware that does not recreate the transport. Also reduce retry attempts to 2 temporarily.

timothy: Internal note for eng-runtime: track this class of issue — we should add an example in docs for "Using context + http.Client correctly" and a snippet showing token refresh without transport recreation. Tagging @eng-runtime for a follow-up.

infra-bot: Created incident INC-2026 and link to support ticket ST-9876.

maria: I'll gather repro + config and reopen if upgrade doesn't help. Thanks folks :pray:
